parts:
Dear Nimble-Users

I am attempting to write a meta-population version of an epidemiological SIR model (for chicken farms). At each population S and R are integer vectors (there are sub-stages to track the age of chickens) and I is an integer matrix. I am trying to use a nimbleFunctionList to store this information. 

My difficulties concern simply writing to and extracting the various vectors and matrices of each population. 

The R version of the code behaves as expected, but I am facing various issues when compiling. I attach a script to demonstrate. The symptoms are 

line 124) the run function returns "NULL"
line 126 & 146) the run functions return "Error: attempt to apply non-function"
line 136) the SetS function returns "Error: attempt to apply non-function"
lines 144) the setS function returns "NULL"

Also, if I uncomment line 47, the compilation step results in error (pasted below).

So... 
Why is the compiled code not working as the R code? 
Why the compilation error? 
How to adjust this code to bypass these difficulties? 

Best regards
David

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Compilation difficulties using nimbleFunctionList for meta-population data structure
parts:
David, it's good to hear from you, and I'm glad you're still moving forward with SIR models in NIMBLE.  I took a look at your code.  There were 2 things not working for you.

(1) In order to access compiled nimbleFunctionLists, and elements within them, and methods within them (including the run method), and the same goes for variables and methods within compiled objects in general, you'll need to set the nimble system option:

nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)

This will allow accessing methods, variables, etc, internal to *compiled* nimbleFunctions, for example:

cStates$StatesInPopList[[1]]$run() # DT: works

Without setting that nimble system option, it's still possible to "dig into" nested compiled objects - it's just more unwieldy and unintuitive.  If that becomes a priority, since compilation will be somewhat slower after setting this option, then take a look in the User Manual (section 15.4.10 it looks like) and search for "valueInCompiledNimbleFunction".

I added this option to your code (modified), which is attached.

(2) The other thing that wasn't working for you - NIMBLE isn't quite always as general as we might hope, or it might seem.  In this case, access to arbitrary elements of the nested nimbleFuntionList object (StatesInPopList) isn't available as "random access" as we might like.  That is, I don't think you can just pass in a **run-time** argument ("pop"), and then access *only* the pop-th element in the list (that is, StatesInPopList[pop] ).

Instead, I think you'll always have to iterate over the entire list as:
for(i in 1:nPops) {     ## DT
    ... arbitrary code involving: StatesInPopList[[i]]
}

So, just a little careful thinking will get around this problem, although I admit it's a "work-around".  See the modified script attached, where I just added a conditional check inside this loop, for whether (i == pop) on each loop iteration.

Anyway, I think the modified script, attached, should get you working.  Like I said, you could find some performance gains from *not* using the nimble option mentioned above; or, if the "looping" I introduced becomes a problem (which I hope might not happen), then we could talk about other options there, also.

Keep at it!

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Compilation difficulties using nimbleFunctionList for meta-population data structure
parts:
Hi David and Daniel,

I took a look at this.  There is an easier workaround to the indexing issue.

First, the warnings about needing to define pop before compilation are misfires of the static code processing that tries to give helpful tips.  We'll have to fix that, but you can ignore it.

Second, the problem using pop as the index arises only for 

StatesInPopList[[pop]]$run(), not for the other method calls.

An easier workaround than Daniel's is simply
i <- pop
StatesInPopList[[i]]$run()

A brief explanation:
nimble does name-mangling of arguments.  For example, "pop" will become "ARG1_pop_".  This makes it possible to support the use of "log" as an argument name.  In R, even the name of a base R function like log can be re-used, and it commonly is in distribution functions that take "log = TRUE".  In C++, one can't use a language keyword like log as an argument name, so we mangle argument names to avoid that conflict.  However that means that we need to replace "pop" everywhere with "ARG1_pop_".  Evidently that is not working for "StatesInPopList[[pop]]$run()", which can be seen by inspection of the generated C++ (not something most people want to do, I know!).  Given that it works for the other method calls, this case where it fails must be due to some quirky oversight or corner case.  In the workaround, the name mangling replacement works for the simple "i <- pop" and then "i" works in "StatesInPopList[[i]]$run()" 

Attached is the simpler version that works.

Thanks again for turning up these issues.  I'll file two bugs arising from this.

-Perry
